[2026-09-13T10:44:01+00:00] THREE TRAPS IT PAID FOR, all of them worth another agent's attention. (1) THE runtime/ground.ts HELPERS CANNOT SEE INSIDE A ROOM: they are built on landableAtScreen, which resolves the front-most drawn surface out of the RAW world rows and knows nothing about the cut-away — measured over 64 points of one chamber it said yes to ONE, while pickAt + surfaceAt found 22 dry floor points, 21 on the player's own terrace. Every indoor placement asks the PICKER (pickGround starts its scan at indoorTop). (2) A SPRITE FACTORY THAT TAKES A DEPTH MUST APPLY IT: mine took one and never called setDepth, so every drop sat at Phaser's default 0, under the darkness overlay at 900_000, and a cave painted them out — 4 spouts, alpha 1, rings spreading, and 0.6 luma on the screen. debug().draw now reports the live sprite's own depth/size/texture and the gate fails at or below 900_000. (3) A PIXEL ARM MUST NOT CHASE A MOVING MARK: passing coordinates from the page to the gate is a race the effect wins (a falling drop covers 24 px between the read and the shot, and even a stationary one is only all[0] until a sibling wakes) — it measured bare rock at 0.0 while a neighbourhood search found the same drop at 157 one pixel away. Judge the largest departure ANYWHERE in the game area over several ON frames, same box for the control. Two more: 'the screen went quiet' can never be true with the player on it (their idle and TORCH swing 244 luma a frame in a dark chamber — skip their box, the precondition is about the GROUND finishing its slices), and A GATE THAT WALKS SOMEWHERE UNUSUAL PUTS THE PLAYER BACK, because the game persists where you logged out and verify-indoor-ambient then fails its first assertion on a clean tree.

[2026-09-13T13:12:03+00:00] FIRE SMOKE SHIPPED (607539cb5), his pick from the ten: 'thin grey wisps curling up from open flames, so a fire reads as burning by day too'. A COLUMN, not a cloud — puffs leave the same point a tenth of a second apart, lean on the cloud wind the pollen and leaves use, bend together on a shared curl phase (neighbours take the last puff's phase plus a step, so the ribbon bends as one instead of scattering), gather 1px->3px and thin away. Only over an OPEN fire: the scenery domain's published light KIND, `fire/*` and not `fire/enclosed`. Keyed on the KIND and NOT on the `embers` boolean even though the two pick the same 82 pieces today — that flag means 'throws sparks', and a smouldering kiln that sparks nothing must still smoke. Sorts against its own fire's litDepth (the embers' law) and draws NORMAL, never additive. Measured at an outdoor brazier (217,234): 15 puffs, 6238 samples above the flame and 0 below, 63px of climb, 36px of curl, 0 over a lantern, unforced weight 1 by day / 0.3 at night, 0.068 ms/frame, 23.9 luma against 0.0 with it off.

[2026-09-13T13:12:03+00:00] THREE TRAPS FROM THE SMOKE, worth another agent's attention. (1) WHICH COLOUR IS DECIDED BY WHAT IS BEHIND IT, not by what the thing is. I painted smoke pale because smoke is pale; over the sunlit ground where 44 of the 51 open fires stand, a 150-grey wisp moved its own pixels by 5.8 luma. The tint now DARKENS as the sun rises (112 at night, 72 at noon) and reads at 23.9. It is the crawlers' rule again — an ant is never pale, a night spider is never white. And 'thin' is the COLUMN, not the mark: the peak alpha went 0.34 -> 0.5 in the same fix. (2) A REPORT A GATE READS IS NOT ALLOWED TO LIE: each puff stored its fire as an INDEX into the list lightsInView rebuilds twice a second, so debug().all reported heights above a flame at the world origin — the gate read a 16,520px wide column while the drawing was correct throughout. Anything a mark is measured against travels ON the mark, captured at birth. (3) A gate in MANUAL mode cannot measure a day/night rule: the toggles FORCE an enabled field on regardless of its env gate, so `gain` reads 1 at midnight — the feature publishes its UNFORCED weight for the gate to assert on.

[2026-09-13T13:12:03+00:00] TWO GATE LAWS, applied to verify-drips as well as the new verify-firesmoke, and in ambient/README.md. THE CLEAR AREA IS MEASURED OFF THE DOM, NEVER GUESSED: every gate here carried a hand-picked box and each is wrong for the next feature — the butterflies' canvas starts below the clock, a cave drip HANGS at y=11, so every window verify-drips sampled was rejected and it read 0.0 luma on a working effect. The canvas is the game area, the HUD is DOM over it (23 rects at 480x320: the bars top-left and top-right, the wiki button), and the elements report their own rects; skip anything covering ~all of the canvas (the wrapper), and check the WHOLE window where the window is chosen, because a window overlapping an excluded rect silently scores 0 and reads exactly like an invisible effect. AND THE CONTROL IS THE QUIET PRECONDITION: 'wait for the screen to go quiet' measures the wrong thing twice for per-mark windows — a monster crossing the chamber blocked the gate at 68.6 luma on a run whose own windows read 0.0. Assert the SAME windows with the effect off instead. If a wide box is genuinely needed, gate it on a PERCENTILE, never the maximum. verify-drips now reads 143.4 against 0.0 and is no longer luck.
